subject: [COMPANY]'s AI Pipeline
text:
[NAME], 

There's a pattern we keep seeing with ML teams at your stage: engineers burning sprint cycles on a pipeline stage that isn't the actual constraint. 

Labeling is usually the first thing to get attention; it's measurable, the team can point to output, and it's easy to staff up. But when we map the pipeline, the real throughput bottleneck is in curation or validation far more often than anyone expects. Model performance doesn't move. Nobody can explain why. 

We built a diagnostic that identifies which stage it actually is for your setup; maps across curation, labeling, QA, and validation, and generates a fix-priority report. 

If that's useful, I'll send it over.

subject: Woven - data visualisation & curation
text:
Hey [NAME]​,

We've recently started working with Woven, Wayve, and Oxa - so thought it could be interesting to reach out to explore if we can help at [COMPANY] in a similar way.

The common challenges these teams faced were around existing data visualisation / curation solutions (Voxel51 & internal tools), lacking the speed & scalability required to efficiently visualise their training datasets (struggling beyond ~1m frames).

At Encord, we've built a high-performance architecture to support indexing / searching through billions of data items (using embeddings visualisations, quality metric filters, & natural language searches), enabling AV teams to avoid bottlenecks in model development.

Would love to chat / share some ideas based on what we've been learning from working with Woven, Wayve, Oxa and similar partners in the space.

Would it be worth us connecting?

subject: Is your 3D data pipeline slowing model development?
text:
Hi [NAME],

I've noticed that many of the to ML teams I speak to in the physical AI space find 3D cuboid labeling to be a big bottleneck in their pipeline.

As point cloud datasets grow, drawing cuboids frame by frame turns into a slow, expensive grind and it's hard to scale.

So we're hosting a short, 20-minute masterclass on the 19th of Feb to walk through how teams are moving away from manual-first 3D annotation and into autolabeling workflows, where models generate cuboids and humans focus on review, fixes, and edge cases.

You can save your spot here: [LINK] Or, if you can't make it live, sign up: [LINK] anyway and we'll send you the recording.
